questions.text: G  is an undirected graph with vertex set {v1, v2, v3, v4, v5, v6, v7} and edge set {v1v2, v1v3, v1v4 ,v2v4, v2v5, v3v4, v4v5, v4v6, v5v6, v6v7 }. A breadth first search of the graph is performed with v1 as the root node. Which of the following is a tree edge?
questions.solution:
BFS from v1 first visits all neighbours of v1: v2, v3, v4. So v1v2, v1v3 and v1v4 are tree edges.
v2v4, v3v4 join two vertices already at level 1, and v4v5 is not used if v5 is first discovered from v2.

Answer: v1v4

questions.text: Graph G is obtained by adding vertex s to [latex]K_{3,4}[/latex] and making s adjacent to every vertex of [latex]K_{3,4}[/latex]. The minimum number of colours required to edge-colour G is _______
questions.solution:
s is joined to all 3 + 4 = 7 vertices, so deg(s) = 7, and the edges at s need 7 different colours. So at least 7 colours.

7 is enough: give s's edges colours 1-7. Each vertex of [latex]K_{3,4}[/latex] has degree at most 5 in G and has already used one colour, and the [latex]K_{3,4}[/latex] edges can be coloured with the remaining colours.

Answer: 7

questions.text: For n[latex]\gt[/latex]2, let [latex]a \in \{0,1\}^n[/latex] be a non-zero vector. Suppose that x is chosen uniformly at random from [latex]\{0,1\}^n[/latex]. Then, the probability that [latex]\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_ix_i[/latex] is an odd number is______
questions.solution:
Pick an index j with [latex]a_j=1[/latex]. For any fixed values of the other [latex]x_i[/latex], flipping [latex]x_j[/latex] changes the parity of the sum. So exactly half of all x make it odd.

Answer: 0.5

questions.text: The number of permutations of the characters in LILAC so that no character appears in its original position, if the two L's are indistinguishable, is ______.
questions.solution:
Positions: 1 L, 2 I, 3 L, 4 A, 5 C. The two L's cannot use positions 1 or 3, so they take 2 of {2, 4, 5}:
- L's at {2, 4}: I, A, C fill 1, 3, 5 with C not at 5 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 3! [latex]-[/latex] 2 = 4
- L's at {2, 5}: fill 1, 3, 4 with A not at 4 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 4
- L's at {4, 5}: fill 1, 2, 3 with I not at 2 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 4

Total = 12

Answer: 12

questions.text:
Which one of the following predicate formulae is NOT logically valid?
Note that W is a predicate formula without any free occurrence of x.
questions.solution:
Since x is not free in W:
- [latex]\forall x(p(x)\vee W)\equiv\forall x\,p(x)\vee W[/latex] [latex]\text{---}[/latex] valid.
- [latex]\exists x(p(x)\wedge W)\equiv\exists x\,p(x)\wedge W[/latex] [latex]\text{---}[/latex] valid.
- [latex]\forall x(p(x)\rightarrow W)\equiv\forall x(\neg p(x)\vee W)\equiv\neg\exists x\,p(x)\vee W\equiv\exists x\,p(x)\rightarrow W[/latex], not [latex]\forall x\,p(x)\rightarrow W[/latex] [latex]\text{---}[/latex] not valid.
- [latex]\exists x(p(x)\rightarrow W)\equiv\neg\forall x\,p(x)\vee W\equiv\forall x\,p(x)\rightarrow W[/latex] [latex]\text{---}[/latex] valid.

Answer: Option 3
